language.label: Language
language.help: The language the game's words are written in. Others come as they are translated.

textSpeed.label: Text speed
textSpeed.help: How fast what people say is written out. The A button always finishes a line at once.

quality.label: Graphics quality

help.High: Sharpest picture: the 3D scenes render at 4K (3840 × 2160) with soft shadows and ambient occlusion.
help.Medium: 3D scenes render at 2880 × 1620 with anti-aliasing; keeps soft shadows and ambient occlusion.
help.Low: Fastest: 3D scenes render at 1920 × 1080 with simple shadows, no ambient occlusion or depth of field.

quality.measured: Measured on this computer at the first start: {quality}, {ms} ms a frame.

help.window: The window's size, in your monitor's own shape ({ratio}).
help.fullscreen: How many pixels the 3D scenes are drawn at in full screen. Native is the sharpest; a smaller one is quicker.

vsync.label: V-Sync
vsync.help: Matches the display's refresh rate to avoid tearing.

help.fixed: The world stays at this time of day.
help.clock: Follows your computer's clock, like the original: morning from 4, day from 10, twilight from 17, night from 20.

sound.label: Sound
sound.help: Music and sound effects (also the M key).

music.label: Music
music.help: How loud the music and the fanfares play.

soundEffects.label: Sound effects
soundEffects.help: How loud the sound effects play: menus, doors, footsteps, the moves in battle.

cries.label: Cries
cries.help: How loud the Pokémon's cries play.

ambience.label: Ambience
ambience.help: How loud the field's background sounds play: rain, wind, waterfalls, the sea, caves.

help.Stereo: Full sound, for speakers or headphones.
help.Handheld: Sounds as the handheld's own small speakers would: no deep bass, a narrow stereo and ten-bit sound.
help.Mono: Everything in one channel, the same in both ears: for a single speaker, or one ear.

moveHints.label: Move hints
moveHints.help: In battle, a move's card says whether it is super effective, not very effective or has no effect on a Pokémon you have seen before.

trainerLines.label: Trainers speak
trainerLines.help: In battle, Gym Leaders, your rival and other bosses say a line when their last Pokémon comes out, when their first one falls and when their last one is in the red.

help.on: A line on the start menu, the Trainer Card and the save's summary says where the story goes next, and Mom and the Pokémon Center nurse remind you when asked.
help.off: Nothing says where the story goes next: you find your own way, as in the original.
A battle's commands are FIGHT, BAG, POKéMON and RUN, chosen by you every turn.
help.on: The commands have AUTO, which plays the battle for you with each Pokémon's strongest move until one of yours faints or Back stops it.

help.off: The menu keeps no list of the errands people give you.
help.on: Once someone asks something of you, the menu has REQUESTS: what each errand needs next, and one you can pin over the field.

help.Off: No tips are shown. Those already shown can still be read on the HELP page.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules show no tips; the modern rules show a few words on something the first time you meet it.
help.On: A few words on something the first time you meet it: a status condition, a tree in the way, a Pokémon Center. Each is shown once, and HELP keeps them.

help.off: A battle lost sends you back to the last Pokémon Center with some of your money gone.
help.on: A battle lost asks first whether to try again: the battle starts over, with what you used and spent in it given back.

help.off: Your Pokémon stay in their balls in the field.
help.on: The first Pokémon of your team that can fight walks behind you. Talk to it to see how it feels.

help.hidden: Wild Pokémon hide in the grass and the water until they jump out at you.
help.visible: Wild Pokémon are seen in the grass and on the water, and you meet only those you walk into.

help.region: You move as each region lets you: four ways on its paths, or more where a region allows it.
help.fourWays: You always move four ways, a step at a time along the paths, whatever the region allows.

help.Off: Nobody's lines are spoken: the text shows alone, as in the original.
help.Story: The story's named characters speak their lines aloud; everyone else's show as text.
help.All: Everyone who has a voice speaks their lines aloud. Lines without one show as text.

voiceVolume.label: Voice volume
voiceVolume.help: How loud the characters' voices speak, on their own, apart from the music's volume. 100 is the normal level and 200 is twice as loud. The music and the ambience dip while someone speaks.

help.off: A on a finished line goes on at once and cuts its voice short.
help.on: A on a finished line waits until its voice has finished speaking.

help.off: In a language with no voices of its own, the lines show as text alone.
help.on: In a language with no voices of its own, the characters speak English under the translated text.

help.off: The place's sign shows only its name.
help.on: The place's sign and the menu count the items, trainers and Pokémon you can still find where you are now, without naming them.

boxesAnywhere.label: Boxes anywhere and a sorted bag

help.Off: The PC's boxes are reached only at a PC, and the bag keeps its items in the order you took them.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules keep both as they are; the modern rules add BOXES to the start menu where the place allows it, and let each pocket of the bag be put in order.
help.On: The start menu has BOXES, which opens the PC anywhere the place allows it, and each pocket of the bag can be put in order by name or by how many, with a letter jump.

help.Off: Hidden items lie unseen, as in Platinum: look at the ground, or use a dowsing app, to find them.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules keep hidden items unseen; the modern rules let one within three steps glint now and then.
help.On: A hidden item within three steps of you glints every couple of seconds, until it is found.

help.Off: A Pokémon's menu in the team has only its summary, its field moves and SWITCH.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules keep the menu as it is; the modern rules add REMEMBER, which teaches back a move it has forgotten, and RENAME.
help.On: A Pokémon's menu in the team also has REMEMBER, which teaches back a move it could have learned by now for nothing, and RENAME for your own Pokémon.

help.Off: Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, Defog, Rock Smash, Waterfall and Rock Climb need a Pokémon on the team that knows them.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules keep the HMs as they are; the modern rules let a wild helper do those eight moves once you have the Badge and the HM.
help.On: With the Badge and the HM in the bag, a wild helper does Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, Defog, Rock Smash, Waterfall and Rock Climb for you.

help.on: While another window is in front, the game waits where it is and its sound drops; it goes on when you come back to it.
help.off: The game runs on, sound and all, while another window is in front.

help.capped: The most frames the game draws a second. V-Sync, when it is on, still holds it to the display's refresh rate.
help.none: The game draws as many frames a second as it can. V-Sync, when it is on, still holds it to the display's refresh rate.

help.Off: Every scene of the story plays through, as in Platinum.
help.Seen: Hold the menu button for a second to skip a scene of the story you have already seen to its end, in this game or another on this computer. Questions and battles are never skipped.
help.Any: Hold the menu button for a second to skip any scene of the story, seen or not. Questions and battles are never skipped.

help.on: Moves and the battle's other animations play, as in Platinum.
help.off: No moves or other animations play in battle: the lines and the HP bars alone, for quicker battles.

help.Shift: When a trainer's Pokémon faints, you are told which comes out next and asked whether to switch first, as in Platinum.
help.Set: When a trainer's Pokémon faints, the next one comes straight out and you are not asked to switch.
help.locked: This game's run keeps the battle style on Set. It can't be changed.

help.Off: Holding the run button changes nothing in battles, text and scenes.
help.Double: While the run button is held, battles, text and the evolution scene play twice as fast. Nothing about how they turn out changes.
help.Triple: While the run button is held, battles, text and the evolution scene play three times as fast. Nothing about how they turn out changes.

help.Off: A line of text waits until you press a button.
help.Slow: A line of text goes on by itself after a long pause. A question always waits for your answer.
help.Fast: A line of text goes on by itself after a short pause. A question always waits for your answer.

help.on: You run without holding the run button, which then makes you walk. Needs the Running Shoes.
help.off: You walk, and run while the run button is held.

frame.label: Text frame
frame.help: The frame round the box that lines of text are written in.

help.Normal: The pad's buttons as the game has them: A to confirm, B to go back, the left face button for the registered item, Start for the menu.
help.StartIsX: Start and the left face button change places: the menu is on the face button and the registered item on Start.
help.LIsA: The left shoulder button confirms as A does. The Pokétch's touch is then on the keyboard (I) alone.

stickDeadZone.label: Stick dead zone
stickDeadZone.help: How far the pad's left stick has to be pushed before it walks or moves a cursor. Raise it if the stick drifts, lower it if it feels dull.

gamepad.label: Controller
gamepad.help: Which of the connected controllers the game reads. The keyboard works whichever is chosen.

help.on: With the Vs. Recorder in the bag, a trainer's battle ends with a question: keep it to watch again?
help.off: Only the battles of the Elite Four and the Champion are kept on the Vs. Recorder, as you fight them.

help.None: No game in the console's second slot: the grass holds only Platinum's own Pokémon.
help.game: As if {game} were in the console's second slot: once you have the National Pokédex, two of its Pokémon are met in the grass of the routes that have them.

help.calendar: Unova's seasons follow the calendar, a month each: spring in January, May and September, then summer, autumn and winter.
help.fixed: Unova stays in this season. No other region has seasons.

controls.label: Controls
controls.help: See every key and button, change any of them, and put them back as they were.

jukebox.label: Jukebox
jukebox.help: Play any song the game has played for you, and every sound effect, cry and ambient sound in it.

packs.label: Packs
packs.help: Turn packs on or off, choose the order they load in, and see whose work each one is.

help.on: The game writes itself quietly after a battle, a heal, a Badge, a catch and on coming to a place, into a file of its own beside your saves. A save of your own is never touched. After a crash, CONTINUE offers it.
help.off: The game is saved only when you save it, as in Platinum.

help.on: When a frame runs long, the 3D scene is drawn a little smaller, down to half its size, and grows back once the game runs easily again. The menus and text stay sharp.
help.off: The 3D scene is always drawn at the size the graphics quality gives.
help.unusable: This computer's graphics driver can't be timed, so the scene can't be resized as you play.

help.Off: A press that must come in time, such as reeling in a bite, has its usual moment.
help.Generous: A press that must come in time, such as reeling in a bite, has twice as long.
help.Automatic: The game presses for you as the moment comes: every bite is reeled in. Where a score is set against others, it is only generous.

help.Light: The controller trembles softly at a hit, a catch, a bite and a bump, while it is the one in your hands.
help.Full: The controller trembles at a hit, a catch, a bite and a bump, while it is the one in your hands.

help.off: Flashes over the picture play at their full brightness: a critical hit, lightning, the way into a battle.
help.on: No flash whitens the picture by more than a quarter, and the flashes into a battle are one soft swell.

help.off: Medals are won and kept on the Trainer Card without a word.
help.on: A medal won drops in at the top of the field with a fanfare.

help.Off: The run is timed in every game, but no corner shows it and no splits are written.
help.HallOfFame: A corner shows the run's time; splits.json beside the save times the Hall of Fame alone.
help.Badges: A corner shows the run's time; splits are taken at every Badge and the Hall of Fame.
help.Story: A corner shows the run's time; splits at every Badge, each Team Galactic commander and the Hall of Fame.

help.Off: Nothing is written for a stream.
help.File: The run is written to stream/state.json beside the save as it changes, for an OBS browser source (stream/overlay.html). Nothing is sent anywhere.
help.FileAndSplits: As a file, and stream/livesplit.lss, a LiveSplit splits file, is kept up as splits are taken.

help.off: Trainer IDs and your folder's name show as they are.
help.on: Trainer IDs are hidden and your folder's name is left out of the log's paths.

help.off: Whoever battles beside you chooses their own moves.
help.on: Before a battle beside a partner, you are asked whether a friend will choose for them. A second pad answers the friend's turns.

help.Off: CAMP is in the start menu only while a Pokémon walks behind you.
help.Rules: Platinum's rules keep the start menu as it is; the modern rules add CAMP, where you can look after each Pokémon close up.
help.On: The start menu has CAMP, where you can pet, feed, brush and treat each Pokémon of the team close up.

help.Classic: Battles are filmed from one seat, as they always were.
help.Region: Each region films its battles in a manner of its own, from Kanto's quiet seat to Galar's camera that never rests.
help.Lively: Every battle is filmed in Galar's manner: the camera keeps moving while you choose.

help.off: Sounds and cries are heard and not written.
help.on: Every sound and cry is named on screen as it plays: "A door opens", "Starly cries".

help.off: A press answers every question, deleting a save or releasing a Pokémon too.
help.on: Deleting a save, resetting the options or releasing a Pokémon waits for the button to be held a moment.

help.off: The camera shakes and moves in close in battle, menus slide in, and grass and leaves sway in the wind.
help.on: Nothing shakes or punches in, menus appear at once, nothing sways, and the background is never blurred.

help.Normal: Lines in the text box and in battle are written at their usual size.
help.Large: Lines in the text box and in battle are written larger, on up to four rows in the field and three in battle.

help.Normal: The interface's colours are drawn as they are.
help.Protan: Colours shifted for eyes that see little red. Types carry their signs and low HP is hatched.
help.Deutan: Colours shifted for eyes that see little green. Types carry their signs and low HP is hatched.
help.Tritan: Colours shifted for eyes that see little blue. Types carry their signs and low HP is hatched.

help.off: The text box is drawn in the frame you chose.
help.on: The text box and the battle's messages are white on solid black, and types carry their signs.

resetDefaults.label: Reset to defaults
resetDefaults.help: Puts every option back as it is in a new game: the language, the sound, the graphics and the controls. Your saves, and the scenes you have seen, are not touched.

reset.heading: Reset every option?
reset.body: Every option goes back to its default. Your saves are not touched.

help.label: Help
help.help: The type chart, the controls and a few notes for the road. This is version {version}.

disclaimer.owners: This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Creatures Inc. or GAME FREAK inc.
disclaimer.original: Pokémon and its characters are trademarks of their owners. All art, models and music here are original.

recovered.heading: Slot {slot}'s last save was damaged
recovered.body: It couldn't be read, perhaps because the game closed while it was being written. The save made before it has been loaded instead.

damaged.heading: Slot {slot} can't be read
damaged.body: Its save and the one kept before it are both damaged, so that game can't be continued. DELETE A SAVE frees the slot for another.

suspension.heading: Slot {slot}'s battle can't be taken up
suspension.body: The battle left there was fought with the game's data as it was then, and that has changed since. The slot's own save is kept as it is.

noFreeSlot.heading: Every slot holds a save
noFreeSlot.body: A new game needs a slot of its own, and all three are taken. DELETE A SAVE, on this menu, frees one of them.

couldNotDelete.heading: Slot {slot} couldn't be deleted
couldNotDelete.body: Its files are still there: something else may be using them. Nothing was changed; try again once it is closed.

oldSaveNoRoom.heading: An older save was left where it is
oldSaveNoRoom.body: {file} is from before the game had slots, and all three slots hold a save. Once one is deleted, the next start gives it that slot.

oldSaveFailed.heading: An older save couldn't be moved
oldSaveFailed.body: {file} is from before the game had slots and couldn't be given one. It is where it was, untouched; the next start tries again.

packs.heading: Slot {slot} was played with packs
packs.body: Not in use now: {packs}. The game goes on without what they changed; turn them on under OPTIONS, PACKS.
packs.region: The game was saved in {region}, which {pack} adds: without it, the game wakes where it began.

crash.heading: The game stopped unexpectedly
crash.noSave: No game had been saved yet.
crash.reportKept: A report was written to {report}, and the game as it stood was kept beside your save as {file}.

newGame.heading: Start a new game?

blurb.one: It will be saved in slot {slot}. The save you have is kept as it is.
blurb.other: It will be saved in slot {slot}. The saves you have are kept as they are.

newGame.plusBlurb: Slot {slot}. NEW GAME+ carries slot {from}'s Pokédex, boxes and half its money from {region} into a harder journey.

delete.heading: Delete slot {slot}?
delete.unreadable: This save can't be read, nor can the one before it. Deleting it frees the slot.
delete.blurb: {name}, {time} played. The save and its backup are deleted for good.
delete.blurbIn: {name} in {place}, {time} played. The save and its backup are deleted for good.

autosave.heading: Take up slot {slot} from its autosave?
autosave.blurb: The autosave is at {place}, {auto} played. The save you made yourself stopped at {saved}.

start.noBoxLink: The boxes can't be reached from here.

quit.heading: Quit the game?
quit.body: Anything since your last save will be lost unless you save first.

objectives.downstairs: Go downstairs. Mom is wondering where you have got to.
objectives.rivalHome: Look in on {rival} next door. He is in a great hurry about something.
objectives.route201: Follow {rival} up Route 201, where Professor Rowan is waiting by the tall grass.
objectives.shoes: Take your new Pokémon home and show Mom.
objectives.lake: Find {rival} at Lake Verity, up the path north of Twinleaf Town.
objectives.lab: Go south to Sandgem Town and Professor Rowan's lab.
objectives.parcel: {rival}'s mother has a parcel for him. Look in at home.
objectives.school: Take the parcel to {rival}, who was heading for Jubilife's Trainers' School.
objectives.poketch: Collect three coupons around Jubilife City and trade them for a Pokétch.
objectives.roark: Go east through Oreburgh Gate to Oreburgh City and win the Coal Badge from Roark.
objectives.worksKey: Go on to Floaroma Town. Team Galactic is up to something in the meadow.
objectives.forest: Take back the Valley Windworks, then work through Eterna Forest to Eterna City.
objectives.gardenia: In Eterna City, win the Forest Badge from Gardenia.
objectives.galacticBuilding: Team Galactic has taken over a building in Eterna City. Go and see what they want.
objectives.bicycle: Pick up a Bicycle at Eterna City's cycle shop.
objectives.fantina: Ride the Cycling Road to Hearthome City and win the Relic Badge from Fantina.
objectives.maylene: Veilstone City is east, past Route 215. Win the Cobble Badge from Maylene.
objectives.wake: Go south to Pastoria City and win the Fen Badge from Crasher Wake.
objectives.oldCharm: Take the Old Charm Cynthia gave you to the elder in Celestic Town.
objectives.ironIsland: Byron has gone to Iron Island. Sail there from Canalave City.
objectives.byron: Win the Mine Badge from Byron in Canalave City.
objectives.lakes: Trouble is brewing at the lakes. Start at Valor Lakefront.
objectives.candice: Snowpoint City lies far in the north. Win the Icicle Badge from Candice.
objectives.storageKey: Team Galactic's trail leads to Veilstone City and its warehouse.
objectives.headquarters: Fight your way through Team Galactic's headquarters.
objectives.coronet: Climb Mt. Coronet. Team Galactic is heading for Spear Pillar.
objectives.spearPillar: Stop Cyrus at Spear Pillar, and follow Cynthia wherever it leads.
objectives.volkner: Sunyshore City, far to the east, is the last Gym. Win the Beacon Badge from Volkner.
objectives.beach: There is more waiting for you on Sunyshore City's beach.
objectives.victoryRoad: Head for Victory Road and the Pokémon League.
objectives.leagueGuard: Show the guard at the League's door your Badges, and mind {rival}.
objectives.champion: Face the Elite Four and the Champion.
objectives.afterwards: Sail from Snowpoint City to the Battle Zone, or see what stirs at Stark Mountain.
objectives.free: Nothing presses. The Battle Frontier, the Battleground and Pal Park are open to you.
objectives.kantoSetOut: Set out from Pallet Town along the road north.
objectives.kantoStarter: Choose a Pokémon from the three on Professor Oak's table.
objectives.kantoRivalLab: {rival} won't let you leave the lab without a battle.
objectives.kantoParcel: Go north to Viridian City and look in at its Poké Mart.
objectives.kantoParcelHome: Take the Mart's parcel back to Professor Oak in Pallet Town.
objectives.kantoBrock: Go through Viridian Forest to Pewter City and win the Boulder Badge from Brock.
objectives.kantoMisty: Cross Mt. Moon to Cerulean City and win the Cascade Badge from Misty.
objectives.kantoBill: Visit Bill at his cottage on the cape north of Cerulean City.
objectives.kantoSurge: Head south to Vermilion City and win the Thunder Badge from Lt. Surge.
objectives.kantoErika: Make your way to Celadon City and win the Rainbow Badge from Erika.
objectives.kantoHideout: Team Rocket is up to something under Celadon City's Game Corner.
objectives.kantoTower: Climb the Pokémon Tower in Lavender Town.
objectives.kantoKoga: Go south to Fuchsia City and win the Soul Badge from Koga.
objectives.kantoSilph: Team Rocket has taken over Silph Co. in Saffron City. Drive them out.
objectives.kantoSabrina: Win the Marsh Badge from Sabrina in Saffron City.
objectives.kantoBlaine: Cross the sea to Cinnabar Island and win the Volcano Badge from Blaine.
objectives.kantoGiovanni: Viridian City's Gym is open at last. Win its Badge.
objectives.kantoLeague: Take Victory Road to the Pokémon League on Indigo Plateau.
objectives.kantoSevii: Celio on One Island could use your help across the Sevii Islands.
objectives.kantoFree: Nothing presses. Kanto and its islands are yours to explore.
objectives.johtoMom: Go downstairs. Mom has something for you.
objectives.johtoElm: Visit Professor Elm's lab next door and choose a Pokémon.
objectives.johtoMrPokemon: Run Professor Elm's errand: find Mr. Pokémon's house past Cherrygrove City.
objectives.johtoBackToElm: Hurry back to Professor Elm's lab in New Bark Town.
objectives.johtoFalkner: Go north to Violet City and win the Zephyr Badge from Falkner.
objectives.johtoBugsy: Go south to Azalea Town and win the Hive Badge from Bugsy.
objectives.johtoWhitney: Go through Ilex Forest to Goldenrod City and win the Plain Badge from Whitney.
objectives.johtoMorty: Head north to Ecruteak City and win the Fog Badge from Morty.
objectives.johtoChuck: Go west to Olivine City, then cross the sea to Chuck's Gym in Cianwood City.
objectives.johtoJasmine: Back in Olivine City, win the Mineral Badge from Jasmine.
objectives.johtoMahogany: Something is wrong at the Lake of Rage, north of Mahogany Town.
objectives.johtoPryce: Win the Glacier Badge from Pryce in Mahogany Town.
objectives.johtoRadioTower: Team Rocket has taken over Goldenrod City's Radio Tower.
objectives.johtoClair: Go through the Ice Path to Blackthorn City and win the Rising Badge.
objectives.johtoLeague: Head west by Route 27 and Victory Road to the Pokémon League.
objectives.johtoKanto: Kanto's Gyms wait across the sea. The S.S. Aqua sails from Olivine City.
objectives.johtoFree: Nothing presses. Johto and Kanto are yours to explore.
objectives.hoennNeighbours: Say hello to the new neighbours next door.
objectives.hoennBirch: Someone is calling for help on Route 101, just north of town.
objectives.hoennRival: Find {rival} on Route 103, north of Oldale Town.
objectives.hoennPokedex: Go back to Professor Birch's lab in Littleroot Town.
objectives.hoennRoxanne: Go through Petalburg Woods to Rustboro City and win the Stone Badge from Roxanne.
objectives.hoennDevon: Help the Devon Corporation get back the goods that were stolen from it.
objectives.hoennBrawly: Sail with Mr. Briney to Dewford Town and win the Knuckle Badge from Brawly.
objectives.hoennWattson: Go north from Slateport City to Mauville City and win the Dynamo Badge from Wattson.
objectives.hoennFlannery: Climb to Mt. Chimney and on to Lavaridge Town for the Heat Badge.
objectives.hoennNorman: Go home to Petalburg City and win the Balance Badge from your father.
objectives.hoennWinona: Head east past the Weather Institute to Fortree City's Gym.
objectives.hoennTateLiza: Sail east from Lilycove City to Mossdeep City and win the Mind Badge.
objectives.hoennJuan: Find the way into Sootopolis City and win the Rain Badge.
objectives.hoennLeague: Take Victory Road to the Pokémon League at Ever Grande City.
objectives.hoennFree: Nothing presses. Hoenn's land and sea are yours to explore.
objectives.unovaHugh: Step outside. Your neighbour is waiting at his door.
objectives.unovaOutlook: Look for Bianca at the outlook above Aspertia City.
objectives.unovaCenter: Let Bianca show you round the Pokémon Center.
objectives.unovaCheren: Win the Basic Badge at Aspertia City's Gym.
objectives.unovaRoxie: Head on to Virbank City and win the Toxic Badge from Roxie.
objectives.unovaBurgh: Take the ship to Castelia City and win the Insect Badge from Burgh.
objectives.unovaElesa: Go north to Nimbasa City and win the Bolt Badge from Elesa.
objectives.unovaClay: Cross the Driftveil Drawbridge and win the Quake Badge from Clay.
objectives.unovaSkyla: Head on to Mistralton City and win the Jet Badge from Skyla.
objectives.unovaDrayden: Make your way to Opelucid City and win the Legend Badge from Drayden.
objectives.unovaMarlon: Ride the Marine Tube to Humilau City and win the Wave Badge from Marlon.
objectives.unovaChasm: Team Plasma is gathering at the Giant Chasm. Stop them.
objectives.unovaLeague: Go through Victory Road to the Pokémon League.
objectives.unovaFree: Nothing presses. Unova is yours to explore.
objectives.kalosDownstairs: Go downstairs. Mom wants a word.
objectives.kalosDoor: Step outside. The neighbours have come to meet you.
objectives.kalosAquacorde: Go north to Aquacorde Town, where your new friends are waiting.
objectives.kalosHome: Go home to Vaniville Town and show Mom your new partner.
objectives.kalosRoute2: Take the trail north of Aquacorde Town onto Route 2.
objectives.kalosRoute3: Follow Route 3 out of the forest toward Santalune City.
objectives.kalosViola: Win the Bug Badge from Viola at Santalune City's Gym.
objectives.kalosRoute4: Take Route 4 north through the garden to Lumiose City.
objectives.kalosLab: Find Professor Sycamore's laboratory, up the avenue from Lumiose's south gate.
objectives.kalosLysandre: Meet the professor at the café in the north of Lumiose City, past the tower.
objectives.kalosRoute5: Leave Lumiose City by its west gate and follow Route 5 toward Camphrier Town.
objectives.kalosCamphrier: Go on along Route 5 into Camphrier Town.
objectives.kalosPalace: Go north up Route 6 and ask at the palace gate for its flute.
objectives.kalosSnorlax: Wake the sleeping Snorlax on Route 7, south of Camphrier Town, with the palace's flute.
objectives.kalosCyllage: Follow Route 7 to the coast and Route 8 north to Cyllage City.
objectives.kalosGrant: Climb to the Gym at the top of Cyllage City and win the Cliff Badge from Grant.
objectives.kalosRoute10: Leave Cyllage City by its north road and follow Route 10's standing stones to Geosenge Town.
objectives.kalosShalour: Take Route 11 east and north to Shalour City, and climb to the Tower of Mastery on its shore.
objectives.kalosKorrina: Win the Rumble Badge from Korrina at the Gym east of Shalour City's main street.
objectives.kalosMastery: Go back to the Tower of Mastery and see Gurkinn, its master.
objectives.kalosRamos: Take Route 12 to Coumarine City and win the Plant Badge from Ramos.
objectives.kalosPowerPlant: Go north from Coumarine City along Route 13 to the Power Plant, where Team Flare has cut Lumiose's power.
objectives.kalosClemont: Go back to Lumiose City and win the Voltage Badge from Clemont at the top of the Prism Tower.
objectives.kalosValerie: Leave Lumiose by its north gate, take Route 14 to Laverre City and win the Fairy Badge from Valerie.
objectives.kalosOlympia: Follow Routes 15 and 17 east through Dendemille Town to Anistar City, and win the Psychic Badge from Olympia.
objectives.kalosLabs: Go to Lysandre's café in the north of Lumiose City and find the way down to his laboratory.
objectives.kalosFlareHQ: Go to Geosenge Town and find Team Flare's hidden door in the middle of the ring of stones.
objectives.kalosWulfric: Take Route 18 south from Anistar City to Couriway Town, then Route 19 to Snowbelle City and its Gym.
objectives.kalosLeague: Go north from Snowbelle through the woods and the village, along Route 21 and up Victory Road to the League.
objectives.kalosStation: Go to Lumiose Station, past the city's east gate. Professor Sycamore is waiting there.
objectives.kalosKiloude: Take the TMV from Lumiose Station to Kiloude City and find your neighbour on the hill at the north of the city.
objectives.kalosSundial: Meet Professor Sycamore by the great sundial in Anistar City.
objectives.kalosLooker: Visit the Looker Bureau, south of Rouge Plaza in Lumiose City, and see its cases through.
objectives.kalosFree: That is as far as the road runs for now. Kalos is yours to explore.
objectives.alolaMom: Head for the door. Mom has something to tell you.
objectives.alolaDoor: Step outside. Professor Kukui is waiting for you.
objectives.alolaIkiTown: Go north up Route 1 to Iki Town.
objectives.alolaTrail: Look for the girl who ran up the Mahalo Trail, north of Iki Town.
objectives.alolaKahuna: Go back down to Iki Town. The kahuna has come home.
objectives.alolaLab: Visit Professor Kukui's laboratory on the beach, south of your house.
objectives.alolaHauoli: Follow the shore east into Hau'oli City.
objectives.alolaMarina: Walk east through Hau'oli City to the marina's pier.
objectives.alolaFestival: Go back up to Iki Town for the festival.
objectives.alolaVerdant: Take Route 2 north from Hau'oli City to Captain Ilima's trial in Verdant Cavern.
objectives.alolaMeadow: Follow Route 2 north onto Route 3 and look for Lillie in Melemele Meadow.
objectives.alolaHau3: Head back along Route 3. Hau is waiting there.
objectives.alolaGrandTrial: Return to Iki Town for Hala's grand trial.
objectives.alolaSail: Meet Professor Kukui at Hau'oli City's marina and sail for Akala.
objectives.alolaPaniola: Take Route 4 north from Heahea City to Paniola Town.
objectives.alolaRoute5: Follow Route 5 north towards Brooklet Hill.
objectives.alolaBrooklet: Find Captain Lana at Brooklet Hill, west of Route 5.
objectives.alolaRoyal: Take Route 6 east from Paniola Town to Royal Avenue.
objectives.alolaMotel: Head north from Royal Avenue up Route 8's coast.
objectives.alolaWela: Follow Route 7's beach to Wela Volcano Park for Captain Kiawe's trial.
objectives.alolaJungle: Find Captain Mallow in the Lush Jungle, west off Route 8.
objectives.alolaKonikoni: Go through Diglett's Tunnel from Route 8 and on to Konikoni City.
objectives.alolaRuins: Climb Memorial Hill east of Route 9 to the Ruins of Life, where Lillie is waiting.
objectives.alolaOlivia: Return to Konikoni City for Kahuna Olivia's grand trial.
objectives.alolaHano: Go south from Royal Avenue to the Hano Grand Resort.
objectives.alolaAether: Take the ferry from Heahea's pier to Aether Paradise.
objectives.alolaMalie: Take the ferry from Aether Paradise to Malie City on Ula'ula Island.
objectives.alolaHokulani: Climb Mount Hokulani, north of Malie City, to Captain Sophocles' observatory.
objectives.alolaTapu: Follow Route 12 east to Tapu Village, where Captain Acerola waits.
objectives.alolaMegamart: Take Acerola's trial in the old Thrifty Megamart, in Tapu Village.
objectives.alolaPoTown: Go north from Tapu Village to Po Town and face Team Skull's boss.
objectives.alolaNanu: Find Kahuna Nanu in the Shady House in Po Town for Ula'ula's grand trial.
objectives.alolaRescue: Sail to Aether Paradise and bring Lillie out of the head office.
objectives.alolaPoni: Take the ferry to Seafolk Village on Poni Island.
objectives.alolaDulse: Take Captain Dulse's trial in Vast Poni Canyon, north of Seafolk Village.
objectives.alolaHapu: Swim across the strait to Exeggutor Island and meet Kahuna Hapu.
objectives.alolaAltar: Climb the road north of Poni Breakers to the Altar of the Sunne and Moone.
objectives.alolaLanakila: Go east from Tapu Village to Mount Lanakila and climb to the Pokémon League.
objectives.alolaTapuKoko: Something stirs in the Ruins of Conflict at the head of the Mahalo Trail. Go and see Tapu Koko.
objectives.alolaTapuLele: Tapu Lele waits in the Ruins of Life on Akala, past Memorial Hill.
objectives.alolaTapuBulu: Cross Haina Desert, east of Route 13, to Tapu Bulu in the Ruins of Abundance.
objectives.alolaTapuFini: Tapu Fini rests in the Ruins of Hope, out on Poni Breakers.
objectives.alolaTotems: New totems have come to the trial sites: Verdant Cavern, Brooklet Hill, Wela Volcano Park and the observatory.
objectives.alolaUltraAltar: The Lightseekers are waiting at the Altar of the Sunne and Moone on Poni Island.
objectives.alolaUltraHunt: Step into the Ultra Wormhole at the Altar and meet the seven Ultra Beasts in their own worlds.
objectives.alolaMegalopolis: Take the Ultra Wormhole to Ultra Megalopolis and climb Megalo Tower.
objectives.alolaRoyalDome: The Battle Royal Dome on Akala's Royal Avenue is open to Alola's Champion.
objectives.alolaFree: That is as far as the road runs for now. Alola is yours to explore.
objectives.hisuiLaventon: Speak to the man in the long coat on the beach.
objectives.hisuiGather: Bring back the professor's three Pokémon, scattered along Prelude Beach.
objectives.hisuiPartner: Go back to Professor Laventon on the beach.
objectives.hisuiVillage: Follow the path north from the beach to Jubilife Village.
objectives.hisuiWallflower: Wait for the professor at the Wallflower, on Canala Avenue down the west side of the village.
objectives.hisuiHall: Go to Galaxy Hall on Floaro Main Street. Commander Kamado will see you.
objectives.hisuiQuarters: Rest in your quarters, just east of Galaxy Hall.
objectives.hisuiTrial: The Survey Corps' entry trial waits beyond the front gate, in the Obsidian Fieldlands. That is as far as Hisui goes for now.
objectives.galarDownstairs: Go downstairs. Mum has news about Hop.
objectives.galarHop: Hop is waiting in front of the house.
objectives.galarStation: Go up Route 1 to Wedgehurst Station and welcome Leon home.
objectives.galarGate: Find Hop by the gate to the Slumbering Weald, on the west side of Postwick.
objectives.galarWooloo: Follow Hop's Wooloo into the Slumbering Weald.
objectives.galarMum: Go downstairs. Mum has something for the journey.
objectives.galarWedgehurst: Go up Route 1 to Wedgehurst. Hop is waiting there.
objectives.galarMagnolia: Follow Route 2 east of Wedgehurst to Professor Magnolia's house by the lake.
objectives.galarGarden: Hop wants a battle in the professor's garden.
objectives.galarLake: Go down to the lakeside with Hop now the night has come.
objectives.galarTrain: Board the train at Wedgehurst Station.
objectives.galarWildArea: The train stopped short of Motostoke. Cross the Wild Area north to the steps under the city.
objectives.galarRegister: Motostoke at last! Go up the ramp to the stadium and register for the gym challenge.
objectives.galarHotel: Registered! Rest at the hotel on Motostoke's lower terrace before the opening ceremony.
objectives.galarCeremony: The morning of the opening ceremony. Go to Motostoke Stadium.
objectives.galarTurffield: The gym challenge is open. Take the west gate onto Route 3, through the Galar Mine to Turffield.
objectives.galarMilo: Turffield at last. Win the Grass Badge at the stadium on the hill.
objectives.galarRoute5: Hulbury's gym is next. Head north out of Turffield onto Route 5, where Hop is waiting.
objectives.galarNessa: On to Hulbury by the sea. Win the Water Badge at Hulbury Stadium.
objectives.galarMineTwo: Kabu's gym is back in Motostoke. Take Galar Mine No. 2 south from Hulbury.
objectives.galarMarnie: Out of the mine and into Motostoke. Someone is waiting by the east wall.
objectives.galarKabu: Win the Fire Badge at Motostoke Stadium, through Kabu's mission.
objectives.galarHammerlocke: Three badges won. North out of Route 5 over Hammerlocke Hills to Hammerlocke.
objectives.galarVault: Sonia is in the vault on the west side of Hammerlocke.
objectives.galarRoute6: Out of Hammerlocke's west gate onto Route 6, towards Stow-on-Side.
objectives.galarStow: Win the fourth badge at Stow-on-Side Stadium.
objectives.galarMural: Something is happening at the mural on the hill above Stow-on-Side.
objectives.galarOpal: Through Glimwood Tangle to Ballonlea, and win the Fairy Badge from Opal.
objectives.galarFree: That is as far as the road runs for now. Galar from Postwick to Ballonlea is yours to explore.

help.Preset: A set of choices to begin with. Normal changes nothing. Pressing A here starts the game as it stands.
help.Difficulty: Easy and Challenge change how strong trainers are. Challenge also gives the important ones more Pokémon and items.
help.LevelCap: Pokémon stop gaining Exp at the level of the next Gym Leader until you have the Badge.
help.ScaleTrainers: Trainers are raised or lowered to stay near the level of your lead Pokémon.
help.Nuzlocke: A Pokémon that faints is lost for good, and only the first wild Pokémon of each area may be caught.
help.DupesClause: A species you already have, or one that evolves from it, does not use up an area's one catch.
help.ShinyClause: A shiny Pokémon may always be caught, whatever the area's catch.
help.GiftsCount: A Pokémon given to you, or one met in a set place such as a legend's, counts as the area's catch.
help.Monotype: Every Pokémon you use must be of this type.
help.PartyLimit: How many Pokémon you can carry. Any more go to the PC.
help.NoBattleItems: Items cannot be used in battle by either side.
help.NoCenter: Pokémon Centers will not heal your team.
help.NoRunning: You cannot run from wild battles.
help.SetStyle: Battle Style is Set, and the Shift offer is never made.
help.NoLaterMechanics: Nobody can Mega Evolve, use a Z-Move, Dynamax or Terastallize: not you, and not the trainers you meet.
help.NoPowers: The Power Watch uses no power and takes no free one. A meal at the camp still gives its own.
help.Remix: A second take on Sinnoh, written for this game: the important trainers bring teams of their own and the wild Pokémon change, so far more kinds can be caught before the League. The rules and the story stay the same.
help.ShinyOdds: How often a Pokémon is shiny. As the rules say is the game's usual chance.
help.RandomSpecies: Wild Pokémon, trainers' teams, gifts, legends and your partner are other species, the same ones every time for a seed. Evolutions stay in their lines.
help.RandomItems: Items on the ground and handed to you are other items. Key items, HMs and anything the story asks for are never changed.
help.RandomAbilities: Each Pokémon's line has other abilities. A Pokémon whose ability makes its own shape keeps it.
help.RandomMoves: Pokémon learn other moves by level, of about the same power, keeping a move of their own type. Trainers' chosen moves change too.
help.RandomTypes: Each Pokémon's line has other types, the whole line changed alike.
help.Seed: One seed makes one game. Left and right roll another; A types nine digits at most. It is kept on the Trainer Card.
help.Start: Begin the game with these choices. They cannot be changed afterwards.

wild.title: Wild Pokémon
wild.text: A wild Pokémon can be fought, caught or run from. Weaken it first: one low on HP, asleep or paralysed is far easier to catch.

trainer.title: Trainer battles
trainer.text: A trainer's Pokémon can't be caught, and there is no running from a trainer. Win, and the trainer pays you prize money.

fainted.title: A fainted Pokémon
fainted.text: A Pokémon with no HP left has fainted and can't battle. Send in another; a Revive or a Pokémon Center brings it round.

poison.title: Poison
poison.text: A poisoned Pokémon loses HP every turn, and now and then as you walk. An Antidote or a Pokémon Center cures it.

burn.title: Burns
burn.text: A burned Pokémon loses HP every turn, and its physical moves hit only half as hard. A Burn Heal cures it.

paralysis.title: Paralysis
paralysis.text: A paralysed Pokémon is slowed and may be unable to move on its turn. A Paralyze Heal cures it.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.text: A sleeping Pokémon can't move until it wakes, which takes a few turns. An Awakening wakes it at once.

freeze.title: Frozen
freeze.text: A frozen Pokémon can't move until it thaws, which happens by chance. A Fire move thaws it, and so does an Ice Heal.

stats.title: Stat changes
stats.text: Some moves raise or lower a stat for as long as the Pokémon stays in battle. Switching it out sets every change back.

weather.title: Weather
weather.text: Rain strengthens Water moves and sun Fire moves; a sandstorm or hail wears down every Pokémon not of a type that stands it.

field.title: On the field
field.text: Screens, spikes and the like lie over one side of the field for several turns. The battle's information panel tells what is in force.

caught.title: A catch
caught.text: A Pokémon caught joins your team and fills in its Pokédex entry. Its summary is in the POKéMON menu.

toBox.title: The PC's boxes
toBox.text: Your team holds six. A Pokémon caught with a full team goes to a box of the PC, which any Pokémon Center's PC can reach.

levelUp.title: Levels
levelUp.text: Pokémon that take part in a battle gain experience, and grow a level when they have enough. Their stats rise with it.

newMove.title: New moves
newMove.text: A Pokémon knows four moves at most. To learn a fifth it must forget one, or the new move can be let go.

evolution.title: Evolution
evolution.text: Pokémon evolve as they grow, and some by a stone, a trade or other ways. An evolution can be stopped while it happens.

ledge.title: Ledges
ledge.text: You can hop down a ledge but not climb back up it. To come back, look for another way round.

teamFull.title: A full team
teamFull.text: Your team holds six Pokémon at most. Another given to you is sent to a box of the PC instead.

nurse.title: Pokémon Centers
nurse.text: A Pokémon Center heals your team for nothing. After a battle lost, you wake at the last one you visited.

pc.title: The PC
pc.text: A Pokémon Center's PC keeps Pokémon in its boxes. Put them in and take them out again whenever you like.

clerk.title: Poké Marts
clerk.text: A Mart sells Poké Balls, Potions and more. What its counter stocks grows with the Badges you hold.

cutTree.title: Trees in the way
cutTree.text: A thin tree can be cut down by a Pokémon that knows Cut, once you hold the Gym Badge that allows it.

rockSmash.title: Cracked rocks
rockSmash.text: Rock Smash breaks a cracked rock outside battle, once you hold the Gym Badge that allows it.

strength.title: Boulders
strength.text: Strength lets your Pokémon push boulders, once you hold the Gym Badge that allows it. It lasts until you leave the place.

surf.title: Surfing
surf.text: Surf carries you over deep water on a Pokémon's back. Wild Pokémon live in the water too.

rockClimb.title: Rock faces
rockClimb.text: Rock Climb takes you up or down a rough wall of rock, once you hold the Gym Badge that allows it.

waterfall.title: Waterfalls
waterfall.text: Waterfall takes you up a waterfall from the water below it, once you hold the Gym Badge that allows it.

help.title: HELP

about.title: Getting about
about.text: Hold the run button once you have the Running Shoes. Talk to people and read signs with the confirm button: many have something to give or to say about the road ahead.

battle.title: In battle
battle.text: A move of a type the foe is weak to does twice the damage, and one its two types are both weak to four times. The TYPES page has every matchup; the move hints in the options can say it on the move's card.

poketch.title: The Pokétch
poketch.text: Once you have it, put it on the screen and change its app with their buttons, and take it in hand to touch it: the arrows move a cursor over its buttons.

saving.title: Saving
saving.text: Save from the menu whenever you like. A Pokémon Center heals your team for nothing, and the last one you visited is where you wake up after losing a battle.

super.headline: Super effective
super.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does twice the damage.

half.headline: Not very effective
half.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does half the damage.

none.headline: No effect
none.line: A {attack} move does nothing at all to a {defend} Pokémon.

plain.headline: A plain matchup
plain.line: A {attack} move against a {defend} Pokémon does its usual damage.

help.twoTypes: Against two types, both count: ×2 and ×2 make four times, ×2 and ×½ cancel out.

howTo.hurdleDash: Your three run a leg each over seven hurdles. Press {key:confirm} to jump just before a hurdle: land on one and your runner trips. The fastest team through all three legs wins.
howTo.blockSmash: Press {key:confirm} to smash the blocks before you, once each swing is over. Every hit tires your Pokémon: press {key:cancel} to send the next one in while the tired one gets its breath back.
howTo.ringDrop: Push the others off the ring with the arrows and press {key:confirm} to lunge. A knock-off scores, a fall loses points, and whoever falls is replaced by the next of their team.
howTo.relayRun: Your runner laps the track by itself and tires as it goes. Press {key:confirm} to spurt and {key:cancel} to hand over to the next one while the tired one rests. Every lap scores.
howTo.circlePush: Get into the circle with the arrows and keep the others out: press {key:confirm} to lunge. Every moment in the circle scores, twice as much alone. Press {key:cancel} to send in a fresh Pokémon.
howTo.goalRoll: Knock the ball into the other teams' goals with the arrows, and press {key:confirm} beside it to strike it. A goal scores; one into your own goal loses points.
howTo.pennantCapture: Run about the field with the arrows and take the pennants before the others do. Running tires your Pokémon: press {key:cancel} to send the next one in. Bump into another and both stand dazed.
howTo.snowThrow: Point the arrows at a team and press {key:confirm} to throw a snowball. Keep {key:confirm} down to duck a ball coming your way. A hit scores two points, a ball ducked one.
howTo.discCatch: Run along your lane with the arrows to where a disc comes down, and press {key:confirm} to jump for it. A catch in the air scores more. Press {key:cancel} to send in a rested Pokémon.
howTo.lampJump: Your Pokémon bounces by itself. Press {key:confirm} just before it lands to spring higher, and light the lamps the top of each bounce passes. Too soon or too late, and it falls back.

battleRoom.title: Battle Room

blurb.teams: Build teams from nothing: any species, its level, nature, ability, item and four moves it can know. Teams are kept on this machine, apart from every save.
blurb.gauntlet: Take a team against Sinnoh's eight Gym Leaders, the Elite Four and the Champion, one after another, each with the team and levels they have in the story. Your team is made whole before every battle.
blurb.streak: Battle trainers of the Battle Frontier one after another at level 50 for as long as your team keeps winning. Every seven battles they grow stronger.
blurb.puzzles: A battle stopped halfway, with a goal: win this turn, outlast an attack, make a catch. Every roll is fixed, so only the right idea works.
blurb.friends: Fight a friend's trainer at level 50: a trainer file dropped in the trainers folder, or a code pasted from the clipboard. You can send your own teams the same way.
blurb.daily: A round of the Battle Factory drawn from today's date: the same six rentals and the same seven trainers for everyone today. Rent three, trade after a win, and see how far you get. The first run of the day is the one kept.
blurb.versus: Two people at one screen: each picks a team and they battle at level 50. Each chooses in turn behind a curtain, so neither sees the other's choice. Nothing is kept.

training.title: TRAINING
training.free: Drills are free, and as often as you like. Effort counts at once.

howTo.throw: A target slides along the back wall and grows smaller as the drill goes on. Move the aim with Left and Right, and press {KEY:confirm} to throw. The middle scores 3, the blue ring 2, the board 1.
howTo.shot: A target slides along the back wall and grows smaller as the drill goes on. Move the aim with Left and Right, and press {KEY:confirm} to fire a shot of energy. The middle scores 3, the blue ring 2, the board 1.
howTo.guard: Pellets come down three lanes. Step from lane to lane with Left and Right, and press {KEY:confirm} to raise the guard as a pellet arrives. On time scores 2, a little off 1; a pellet let through stuns you for a moment.
howTo.shield: Pellets of energy come down three lanes, faster than in the guard. Step from lane to lane with Left and Right, and press {KEY:confirm} to raise the shield as one arrives. On time scores 2, a little off 1; one let through stuns you.
howTo.sprint: Press {KEY:confirm} on the beat to build up pace; a press off the beat loses some. Hold it down to jump a hurdle. The further you run, and the more hurdles you clear, the higher the score.
howTo.run: A long run on a slower beat. Press {KEY:confirm} on the beat to keep the pace, and hold it down to jump a hurdle. Stamina runs down as you go, and faster with every stumble: with none left you can only crawl.
